First Successful Reception and Decode of a Weather Satellite Image Using an RTL-SDR (more info in comments)

Last night, on my second try, I managed to get this image from NOAA 19. It was deep twilight, so the visual part isn't that clear relative the the infrared part. Nevertheless I'm quite encouraged by the success!

Hardware

  • TV "bunny ears" with telescopic elements angled at 90 degrees from one another. Each element is set to around 54cm in length (resonant at 137MHz if my arithmetic is correct). I replaced the old coax on there with new RG-59U - with a US threaded TV connector. Then used an adapter from that to an SMA plug for the dongle.
  • RTL-SDR dongle (plastic bodied one with the R820T2 receiver and TXCO).
  • USB Male to Female cable (IOW, both ends with the "wide" plug, but one is female) with ferrite EMI supressors clamped on each end.
  • Lenovo Ideapad S210 Touch laptop (Windows 8.1 - x86-64).

Software

  • Dongle driver (don't recall the version).
  • SDR# version 1.0.0.1426.
  • WXtoImg version 2.10.11.
  • Also Orbitron version 3.71 to see what satellites are coming up ahead of time.

Configuration and Setup

I used this page to set up everything. It went without much trouble. Outside, I held the antenna up and oriented it to maximize the signal as I watched SDR#'s spectrum display. It seem to be best when the plane of the V was pointing at the satellite, the position of which I determined from Orbitron's display.

I've used this RTL-SDR on Linux (Centos 6.7) with the Redhawk SDR software to decode SCA on FM, along with the RBDS data. But I must say the satellite image is a high for me! Lots of fun!
